title: Proposal to Review CPF Withdrawal Limit for Singaporeans who Have Not Met Full Retirement Sums in View of Inflation
what_it_is: Proposal to Review CPF Withdrawal Limit for Singaporeans who Have Not Met Full Retirement Sums in View of Inflation

sections.label: CPF withdrawal limit and retirement sums
sections.summary: Raising the $5,000 unconditional withdrawal limit would lower future monthly retirement payouts, so the Government rolled out support measures instead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Increasing the $5,000 unconditional withdrawal limit will only lower members' future monthly retirement payouts, especially for those who have not met their required retirement sum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To help Singaporeans cope with inflation and the rising cost of living, the Government has instead rolled out a comprehensive series of measures to provide immediate and targeted support which have helped the lower-income and the more vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For those who turned 55 from 2013 onwards, they can withdraw up to 20% of their Retirement Account savings from age 65.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Property owners also have the flexibility to set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of property and cash and can thus withdraw their Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum or BRS.

sections.label: Assurance Package cost-of-living support
sections.summary: The Government announced one-off Assurance Package measures: Cost-of-Living Special Payment, Seniors' Bonus, and up to $760 in U-Save Rebates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the immediate cost of living issues, the Government has announced one-off support measures under the Assurance Package at Budget this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, you have got the Cost-of-Living Special Payment of between $200 and $400 for each eligible adult Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Then, there is the Cost-of-Living Seniors' Bonus of between $200 and $300 for eligible Singaporeans aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In total, eligible households can expect to receive up to $760 in U-Save Rebates this year.
